proofs.concat: Let p=2^61-1 and a,b,c in [0,p). Then 0<=x=a*b+c<=(p-1)^2+(p-1)=p^2-p<p^2<2^122. Thus folding F=(x&p)+(x>>61) satisfies 0<=F<=2p-2<2p and F is congruent to x mod p. One conditional subtraction returns a canonical residue. The right_length=0 path retains add(left,right).
proofs.byte_fold: multiply_raw(a,b)<2p for native canonical operands. Adding byte<=255 can exceed 2p, so this rejected candidate performs a second Mersenne fold before its final subtraction. It does not use an invalid single subtraction on raw+byte.
proofs.split_fold: floor(product/2^61)=(uint64(product)>>61)+(uint64(product>>64)<<3), with disjoint source bits and no overflow. Splitting this sum is mathematically exact but can alter instruction latency.

rejected.name: 31bit Karatsuba 3-product standard multiply
rejected.reason: GCC/Clang standard arithmetic is slower by about 2.4%..16.7% across screened operations. Native implementation is identical.
rejected.formula: a=a0+2^31*a1, b=b0+2^31*b1; low=a0*b0, high=a1*b1, cross=(a0+a1)*(b0+b1)-low-high. All three products fit uint64 because a0+a1<3*2^30 and b0+b1<3*2^30. Fold low + cross*2^31 + high*2^62 using 2^61=1. Numeric formula fits the existing 4p raw bound, but added add/sub dependencies negate the saved multiply.

rejected.name: global manual unroll 2/4
rejected.reason: Native/Clang benefits not stable; keep these baseline paths and select only measured GCC standard path.

rejected.name: GCC standard #pragma unroll 4
rejected.reason: Unlike explicit unrolling, GCC chooses schedules with no reliable large-input gain, with small one-byte regressions around 2%..5%.

rejected.name: SSE2 two-stream standard arithmetic build
rejected.reason: Large constructor/clear+assign regressions roughly 9%..31%. 4 packed partial multiplications replace 8 scalar products, but shifts/additions and a joint state dependency defeat scalar instruction-level parallelism.
rejected.guards: __SSE2__ && __x86_64__ && !SIRKIT_DISABLE_SIMD && (!__SIZEOF_INT128__ || SIRKIT_FORCE_STANDARD_ARITHMETIC); activate only size>=256. x86_64 ABI mandates SSE2, so no extra runtime CPU probe is needed. Remaining cases use existing standard loop. GCC native/Clang native are unmodified.
rejected.mathematics: Each 64-bit lane independently carries prefix hash or base power. With 32-bit a0/a1 and b0/b1 compute low=a0b0, cross=a0b1+a1b0, high=a1b1. Fold low + cross*2^32 + high*2^64 with 2^61=1 and 2^64=8; add byte in hash lane only, fold again and conditionally subtract p. All sums stay below 4p+255<2^63; high sign bit of difference detects subtraction underflow. It is mathematically the current standard algorithm run in parallel, with no data rearrangement or probabilistic approximation.

proofs.subject: Native concat fused multiply-add normalization
proofs.argument: Let q=2^61 and p=q-1. Canonical left=a, power=b, right=c each lie in [0,p-1]. z=a*b+c <= p*(p-1)=q^2-3q+2 < 2^122, so __uint128_t cannot overflow. floor(z/q)<=q-3=p-2 and z mod q <=p. Therefore folded=(z mod q)+floor(z/q)<=2p-2, fits uint64_t and requires at most one subtraction of p. q is 1 modulo p, so result is canonical and congruent to a*b+c.

proofs.subject: Concat zero length and empty objects
proofs.argument: right_length==0 follows add(left,right), preserving support for arbitrary canonical hashes (right need not be zero). No powers_ access occurs in this branch, including fresh empty, clear(), and moved-from objects. Positive right_length remains checked against size unless SKIP_RUNTIME_CHECKS, where prior valid-input preconditions apply.

proofs.subject: Four-step construction and assignment recurrence
proofs.argument: Each of the three changed loops preserves ordered byte conversion to unsigned char, ordered hash multiply-add, ordered power multiplication where needed, and the same prefix/power stores. Invariant i<=n is initialized with i=0 and preserved. The guard n-i>=4 establishes i+4<=n, making all reads s[i+j], j=0..3, and stores through index i+4 in the n+1 sized arrays valid. Tail iteration exactly covers n%4 elements. Existing capacity limit remains unchanged and prevents count=n+1 from overflowing.

proofs.subject: assign power reuse and exception guarantee
proofs.argument: reuse_powers is evaluated before resize. If old power_data_ size>=n+1, entries [1,n] remain valid after shrink and the changed reuse loop intentionally writes prefixes only. Otherwise both tables are rebuilt, just as baseline. reserve ordering, resize, non-owning pointer update, allocations, and Entry no-throw initialization are unchanged; arithmetic and stores do not throw. No new exception path is introduced.

proofs.subject: Compiler arithmetic fallback
proofs.argument: Fused concat is enabled exactly for GCC/Clang with __SIZEOF_INT128__ and without SIRKIT_FORCE_STANDARD_ARITHMETIC. Its fallback retains the old multiply/add expression. Four-step loops are enabled only for GCC excluding Clang on x86_64 when 128-bit arithmetic is absent or explicitly disabled. Other compilers/targets retain baseline scalar construction. No ISA-specific instruction or CPU detector is added, hence no new SIRKIT_DISABLE_SIMD interaction.

proofs.subject: API, ownership, and state
proofs.argument: Public signatures, member representation, includes, component guard SIRKIT_ROLLING_HASH_DEFINED, base normalization, get/equal/lcp/compare, copy/move/swap/clear, length validation, and allocation limits are unchanged. Helpers remain private class members. No new macro or namespace leaks, no raw new expression, no source retention or borrowed input ownership.
